original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Authentication success or credential possession must remain distinguishable from the authority of the actual actor and purpose represented by the session.

new_episodes.source_paraphrase: Microsoft filed a civil suit in December 2024. Court orders enabled website seizure; the case was unsealed in January 2025.
new_episodes.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A legal containment action is distinct from model-side prevention.

new_episodes.source_paraphrase: Microsoft reports that network members then blamed and exposed personal information about its counsel. In February it identified four defendants and announced planned criminal referrals.
new_episodes.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Retaliation and planned referrals are later responses, not convictions.

new_episodes.source_paraphrase: The clerk entered default against three defendants on 1 December 2025. On 26 May 2026 a magistrate recommended default judgment and a permanent injunction. Later docket indexes list a grant; the final order was not freshly accessible.
new_episodes.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Entry of default, a recommendation and final relief are distinct judicial stages.

explicit_evidence_changes.old_value: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit reported that Storm-2139 members scraped exposed customer credentials from public sources and used them to unlawfully access accounts with generative-AI services. Microsoft also described a network of creators, providers and users supplying guardrail-bypass tools and enabling illicit AI services; Axios independently reported Microsoft's attribution.
explicit_evidence_changes.new_value: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit reported that Storm-2139 members scraped exposed customer credentials from public sources and used them to unlawfully access accounts with generative-AI services. Microsoft also described a network of creators, providers and users supplying guardrail-bypass tools and enabling illicit AI services; Axios independently reported Microsoft's attribution. Microsoft’s civil action enabled website seizure. It reported later retaliation against counsel and planned criminal referrals. The clerk entered default against three defendants in December 2025. A magistrate recommended default judgment and permanent relief in May 2026; later public docket indexes list a grant.
